full_judgment:
22. The plaintiffs-appellants-petitioners filed suit for declaration of title and for permanent injunction. In such case burden of proof lies on the person who desires any court to give judgment as to any legal right. Section 101 of the Evidence Act runs thus: 

 "Whoever desires any court to give judgment as of any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts must prove that those facts exist. When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person." 

 23. The burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. It is reasonable and just that the suitor who relies upon the existence of a fact should be called upon to prove his own case. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish the case. He cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof. The burden of proving the case is upon the claimant. 

 26. Section 110 of the Evidence Act gives effect to the principle that possession is prima facie evidence of complete title; anyone who intends to oust the possessor must establish a right to do so. This is to be presumed from lawful possession until the want of title or a better title is proved. Possession is prima facie proof of ownership, possession has a two-fold value; it is the evidence of ownership, and is itself the foundation of a right to possession. 

 29. But section 103 of the Evidence Act states that "The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person." when the defendant alleges that he has right, title and interest in the suit property which the plaintiff does not accept. In such circumstances it be Comes a fact which is asserted by the defendant and is denied by the plaintiff. As per section 103 of the Evidence Act, the onus of proving the same is on the defendant. Whenever a person asserts affirmatively as part of his case that a certain state of things is present or is absent, or that a particular thing is insufficient for a particular purpose, that is an averment which he is bound to prove affirmatively. 

 30. Here, in this case, the plaintiffs claim the suit pond firstly by way of lease and alternatively by inheritance showing Gandu Kha as full brother of Mia Kha and both the assertions of the plaintiffs have been proved false. When the assertions of the plaintiffs have not been proved, than as per provision of section 103 of the Evidence Act, the burden rebuts to the defendants. Then we have to see how far the assertions of defendants have been proved. It appears from the evidence on record that the predecessors of the defendant Haji Mia Kha claimed title in suit pond by way of settlement and accordingly, CS record was prepared in the name of Mia Kha, that the heirs of Mia Kha transferred the suit pond to Abdul Mannaf Kha and others and on the basis of this sale deed, SA record was prepared in the name of Abdul Mannaf, Abdul Majid, Nazir Ahmed and Abdul Hamid and the Khatian market Exhibit Ka(1) who also paid rent through rent receipt marked Exhibit 'Ga'. It further transpires from evidence that Abdul Mannaf and others having right, title, interest and possession in the suit pond transferred the same in favour of Md Hanif Mia by a kabala deed No. 13424 dated 7-5-1993 marked exhibit-Gha who also mutated his name through mutation khatian marked Exhibit Kha(2) and Hanif Miah also paid rent by rent receipt marked Exhibit Ga(1). Thus the assertion of the defendants to the effect that they have title and possession in the suit pond has been proved.
